solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, mirror symmetry); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: American navy in Naples moved north

indicators.note: the letters of the words navy in Naples are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A US Navy ship in Naples harbour sets sail northwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' turns NAVYINNAPLES into PENNSYLVANIA; N for 'north' goes on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the US state of Pennsylvania is a Pennsylvanian, so an American by nationality.

clue.text: Plumbism oddly appearing in the locals

indicators.note: oddly says take the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the word Plumbism

explanation.surface: Lead poisoning turns up among the regulars at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Plumbism is lead poisoning; only its odd-placed letters count.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage your local is your neighbourhood bar, so locals are drinking houses.

clue.text: Number any do, possibly twelve

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of any do may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A vague instruction to pick a number, any one, perhaps twelve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twelve' looks like the number being chosen, but it is the definition: twelve o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday falls at twelve o'clock, the hour also called noon or noonday.

clue.text: Nick a result?

definitions.meaning: to nick is to cut a notch or scratch, as one marks a tally
the final tally of points in a game

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether stealing something counts as a success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like British slang for steal, but here it is a notch or cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A notch cut in wood is a scratch mark; a match's final points tally is also called this.

clue.text: News of the French cricket match

parts.note: LA is the French feminine word for the
a Test is an international cricket match lasting several days

explanation.surface: A report on a French cricket fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is the long international form of cricket, a sport popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The most recent report, as in 'have you heard the most up-to-date word?', is news.

clue.text: Case prepared for holiday? Exciting!

parts.note: a legal case or lawsuit is an action
a bag or person ready to travel has been packed

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled that their suitcase is ready for a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' suggests a suitcase, but it is a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A film full of thrills and stunts is described with this compound adjective meaning exciting.

clue.text: So about to drop litter, the swine!

definitions.text: So about to drop litter, the swine!

parts.words: So about to drop litter, the swine!
parts.note: a swine about to give birth to a litter of piglets is a pregnant sow, and 'So' hints at the sow

explanation.surface: An outburst at someone about to drop rubbish: what a swine!
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop litter' sounds like tossing rubbish, but means giving birth to piglets; 'swine' is the creature, not an insult.
explanation.definitionFit: A pregnant sow is described as carrying young, expecting piglets, in farming idiom.

clue.text: They're for gentle decline, rather than going downhill fast

definitions.text: They're for gentle decline, rather than going downhill fast

parts.words: They're for gentle decline, rather than going downhill fast
parts.note: gentle declines are easy ski runs for beginners, not speedy descents; going downhill fast also suggests deteriorating

explanation.surface: A remark about managing a slow fall in health rather than a rapid collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decline' and 'going downhill' read as deterioration, but they are literal gradients on a ski field.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentle beginners' ski runs at a resort are named after a children's room, being for novices.

clue.text: Huge birthday meal? Deal with the candles!

definitions.meaning: a lavish feast or celebration, informally
extinguish the flames on a cake with a puff of breath

explanation.surface: A big birthday dinner, then the cake arrives to be dealt with.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a lavish feast is this; also the phrase for extinguishing flames with a puff of breath.

clue.text: Drinker reflected about something to smoke

indicators.note: reflected, like an image in a mirror, says the letters are read back to front

parts.note: RE means about or concerning, as in letter headings
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A drinker muses on something to smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy habitual drinker is an old word for a boozer or tippler.

clue.text: Plant that's unusual astounded Reg

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters of astounded Reg take an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A man named Reg is amazed by a strange plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fern whose spore spike resembles a snake's forked tongue is the named plant.

clue.text: I cap rate, revised for a hefty fee

indicators.note: revised says the letters of I cap rate are reworked into another order

explanation.surface: A lender boasts of capping the interest rate, but charges heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning obtainable only at considerable cost, so at an expensive charge.

clue.text: Shaking booty next to head of your younger partner

indicators.note: shaking the word booty jumbles its letters
head of means the first letter of the word your

explanation.surface: Someone dancing provocatively beside their much younger lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal term for a much younger man who is the lover of an older person.

clue.text: Supervised and completed cut

parts.note: a finished thing is over
saw means to cut, as with a blade

explanation.surface: A manager watched over and finished the cutting job.
explanation.definitionFit: To watch over and direct people's work is to monitor or manage them; the past tense fits.

clue.text: Become more compassionate, perhaps, or arrogant

definitions.meaning: a whimsical instruction to raise one's compassion, the two words 'up' and 'pity' read as a phrase

explanation.surface: Advice to someone: be kinder, or else stay haughty.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is jokey: 'up' as a verb meaning increase, followed by compassion.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone self-important and presumptuous, acting above their station, is described informally this way.

clue.text: Provides, at home, underclothes

parts.note: being in means being at home
vests are undershirts in British English

explanation.surface: Someone supplies underwear for wearing around the house.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a vest is an undershirt, not a waistcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow someone with power or a quality is to give or supply it to them.

clue.text: Selling agent, maybe, even more hard up?

definitions.meaning: a dealer arranging sales for others, such as of shares
comparative of the slang word for penniless

explanation.surface: A salesman asked if he is now even poorer than before.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockbroker or estate dealer arranges sales; also the comparative of slang for penniless.

clue.text: Some cruets apparently brought back for chemist

indicators.note: brought back says the letters picked out are read in reverse
Some says only part of the words cruets apparently is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Some condiment pots seem to have been returned to the pharmacist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes RUETSAP from the words, and 'brought back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis, the French scientist behind pasteurisation and vaccines, was trained in chemistry.

clue.text: Teams close to abyss on fateful day in Rome

indicators.note: close to means the end letter of the word abyss

parts.note: the Ides of March, when Julius Caesar was assassinated

explanation.surface: Rival teams teeter on the brink of disaster on a doomed Roman day.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposing groups in a match are teams, each one a competing party.

clue.text: Around six fifty, complain

parts.note: CA is short for circa, Latin for around
VI is six in Roman numerals
L is fifty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: At roughly ten to seven, someone starts grumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six fifty' looks like a time but gives the two Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise petty objections and quibble is to grumble about trivial points.

clue.text: River, one west of North Dakota, America

indicators.note: in an across entry, west of means placed to the left, before the next piece

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
ND is the postal abbreviation for North Dakota
US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A river lies just west of North Dakota in America.
explanation.definitionFit: The great waterway flowing through Pakistan to the Arabian Sea is an Asian river.

clue.text: Riotous party in joint with drink

parts.note: the knee is a joint of the leg
to sup is to drink, or a mouthful of drink

explanation.surface: A wild party held in a bar with plenty to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests a bar or club, but is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal name for a lively, noisy celebration with dancing, typically of the old Cockney kind.

clue.text: Direction was rated poorly

indicators.note: poorly suggests the letters of was rated are badly arranged and need reordering

explanation.surface: A film director's work received bad reviews.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Direction' reads as a director's work, but means a compass bearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading toward sunrise is a compass bearing, a way of travel.

clue.text: Deadly reptiles decapitated insects

indicators.note: decapitated means the head, the first letter, is cut off the stinging insects

parts.note: wasps are stinging insects

explanation.surface: Venomous snakes have bitten the heads off some bugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Small venomous snakes, such as the Egyptian cobra Cleopatra used, are deadly reptiles.
